- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly or adjust for mean reversion toward recent lows.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model frequently overcorrects with a steep upward trend; cap forecast growth or introduce lagged decay.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias or adjust for volatility decay.
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome drops sharply, model misses reversal; add early warning signal or adjust for sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; increase sensitivity to sentiment changes in last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.33” values, model tends to be overly conservative; allow slight upward adjustment to reflect latent momentum.
